program: Vaccination access partnerships, education and policy
priceScope: Matched FY2025 full coalition annual cost against partial supported vaccination-channel benefits; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.
formula: Health = (N patients × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted duration − full exposed patient harm) × local share. Completed eligible changed households jointly log net caregiver/adult resources and full access costs. Positive-only overlap and distinct payer/provider loss are retained. Price = 10 × C / combined equivalents.
what: Immunize Colorado supports partner vaccination access, provider education and policy.
The matched 2025 reference uses 440 supported Shots for Tots and Teens patients, not 1,355 vaccines or all partner activity.
Health and signed household resources are assessed without treating outreach as changed uptake or children as immediate wage earners.
strengths: Newest full IRS cost and supported vaccination patient envelope are matched to 2025.
Current clinics and public alternatives identify a concrete access mechanism.
Partner doses, VISTA contacts and statewide education are not summed as unique coalition-caused beneficiaries.
reservations: Vaccine mix, completed protection, residence and coalition additionality remain judgments.
Full coalition costs cover other policy and education channels whose effects are unknown.
The nonprofit's annual cost omits potentially material partner delivery and public vaccine resources.

sections.what: Current support helps partners offer no- or low-cost vaccinations alongside education, VISTA and policy work. The program serves children and some adults; caregiver time is relevant without assigning children's earnings. Coalition-supported delivery is not ownership of every clinical dose.
sections.monitoring: Request unique patient households, age and vaccine mix, completed protective series, doses truly additional to public VFC/insurance access, resident share and partner resource cost. For policy distinguish supported legislation from implemented access, changed uptake and recipient attribution.
sections.qualitative: The 2025 supported Shots for Tots and Teens envelope is 440 patients. Multiple doses do not constitute multiple independent people, and other partner, messenger and VISTA populations may overlap. National/statewide education contacts and policy support are not measured uptake. Those other mechanisms remain unknown rather than zero.
sections.cost: FY2025 full cost $571,433 includes $569,413 functional expense plus $2,020 netted direct event costs. It is paired with 440 supported patients. Unique household conversion .8, completed indicated dose .9, coalition additionality .3, efficacy-response .8 and expected morbidity-equivalent .003 for one year are judgments; no measured recipient QALY conversion or uniform lifetime vaccine benefit is claimed. Denver share .75 is judged from clinic locations, not observed residence. Resource gain comprises $40 net caregiver/adult sick-time/work resources and $10 actually-paid illness cost avoidance after taxes/benefit changes/work costs. Separate .2 resource incidence limits the gained subgroup; this is not a measured adult proportion or child wages. Positive gains receive .5 overlap adjustment. All exposed households retain full $5 travel/time loss and .00002 vaccine/process harm, including failed incremental benefits. Central external partner/public loss zero is a limitation; sensitivities assess provider/payer/volunteer resources without importing hospital or partner budgets. The $222,806 outreach cost is mixed education, not clinical allocation; a recognized-cost sensitivity cannot establish marginal vaccination price. Health and patient process harms use all 440 patients, without household deduplication. Resources alone use a judged post-dedup household allocation: pediatric caregivers (388/440), adult patients (49/440), and three age-unknown patients whose household units retain burdens but no gains. Caregiver and adult resource incidence can be independently null. The distinct household allocation is a hypothesis, not observed deduplication. Original seasonal placebo-controlled influenza evidence establishes efficacy and dose dependence, not this vaccine mixture's QALYs. Central .003 represents a judged 1.095 expected healthy-day-equivalent per patient before vaccine efficacy for one year. A separate flu-risk illustration uses hypothesized .05 annual infection risk, seven days at .5 utility loss and trial .5098 efficacy; it is not a measured clinic coefficient.
sections.funding: Current own donor page identifies EIN 84-1479975 and links its Neon route; destination could not be rendered by the browser tool and no transaction occurred. Hospital office/email affiliation does not mean its budget is this recipient's. Public VFC, insurance, health departments and other clinics are alternatives. Coalition policy support may change implemented uptake, but the initial reference does not assign an unmeasured statewide policy coefficient.

costScope: Full calendar FY2025 coalition IRS expense including netted direct event costs, against partial supported patient benefit. Partner delivery costs and other channels unmeasured; not full social portfolio EV.
geography: Judged .75 share in pinned ten-county Denver CBSA19740, based on metro clinic anchors but without recipient residence data; statewide activities not fully assigned to Denver. New detailed county counts describe clinic locations (including Boulder), not residence; .75 remains judged.
counterfactual: VFC, Medicaid/private insurance, local public health and other clinical providers without coalition support; access and trust barriers may leave additional patients.
attribution: Judged .3 coalition contribution after alternative access, .9 complete protection and .8 response. Supported patients and doses do not establish changed uptake or causal disease reduction.
uncertainty: Vaccine mix, incidence, age, protection duration, household overlap, local residence, attribution and delivery costs unmeasured. Policy/education/VISTA benefits are unknown, not zero.
native: Original 2025 patient report: 440 patients, including 388 children, 49 adults and three age-missing. Clinic county totals are location, not resident geography; doses and other partner channels not added.

inputRationales.C: Observed full FY2025 original IRS $569,413 plus $2,020 netted direct event expenses.
inputRationales.N: Observed FY2025 supported clinic patient envelope 440; unique household and completion gates are separate judgments.
inputRationales.q: Judged expected morbidity .003 (1.095 healthy-day-equivalents) per patient before vaccine efficacy for one year; mixed vaccine/risk/utility not measured. Seasonal flu risk-duration illustrative sensitivity anchored to original efficacy.
inputRationales.response: Judged .8 mixed-vaccine efficacy applied once to untreated expected morbidity q; q is before efficacy, not already avoided QALYs. Original influenza trial supports only a separately labeled .5098 seasonal sensitivity.
inputRationales.workGain: Judged $40 after-cost adult/caregiver illness-related net resources for separately gated .2 subgroup; no child wages.
inputRationales.medicalGain: Judged $10 actual otherwise-paid illness expenses, not vaccine retail value.
inputRationales.b: Judged .3 coalition-caused additional access beyond VFC/insurance/partners; not ownership of all clinical output.
inputRationales.delay: Judged .1-year clinic engagement start for access cost and protection/resource period together.
inputRationales.unique: Judged .8 income-household deduplication only. Clinical patients and harms remain 440; post-dedup pediatric/adult household allocation is not observed.
inputRationales.childShare: Observed 388/440 child-patient composition; allocation to disjoint deduplicated caregiver resource units remains a hypothesis.
inputRationales.adultShare: Observed 49/440 adult-patient composition; not an observed unique adult household count.
